1	---
2	title: use server
3	description: Learn how to use the use server directive to execute code on the server.
4	---
5	
6	The `use server` directive designates a function or file to be executed on the **server side**. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all functions in the file are server-side, or inline at the top of a function to mark the function as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions). This is a React feature.
7	
8	## Using `use server` at the top of a file
9	
10	The following example shows a file with a `use server` directive at the top. All functions in the file are executed on the server.
11	
12	```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
13	'use server'
14	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
15	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
16	
17	export async function createUser(data: { name: string; email: string }) {
18	  const session = await auth()
19	  if (!session?.user) {
20	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
21	  }
22	
23	  const user = await db.user.create({ data })
24	  return { id: user.id, name: user.name }
25	}
26	```
27	
28	```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={1} switcher
29	'use server'
30	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
31	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
32	
33	export async function createUser(data) {
34	  const session = await auth()
35	  if (!session?.user) {
36	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
37	  }
38	
39	  const user = await db.user.create({ data })
40	  return { id: user.id, name: user.name }
41	}
42	```
43	
44	### Using Server Functions in a Client Component
45	
46	To use Server Functions in Client Components you need to create your Server Functions in a dedicated file using the `use server` directive at the top of the file. These Server Functions can then be imported into Client and Server Components and executed.
47	
48	Assuming you have a `fetchUsers` Server Function in `actions.ts`:
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1} switcher
51	'use server'
52	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
53	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
54	
55	export async function fetchUsers() {
56	  const session = await auth()
57	  if (!session?.user) {
58	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
59	  }
60	
61	  const users = await db.user.findMany({
62	    select: { id: true, name: true, email: true },
63	  })
64	  return users
65	}
66	```
67	
68	```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={1} switcher
69	'use server'
70	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
71	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
72	
73	export async function fetchUsers() {
74	  const session = await auth()
75	  if (!session?.user) {
76	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
77	  }
78	
79	  const users = await db.user.findMany({
80	    select: { id: true, name: true, email: true },
81	  })
82	  return users
83	}
84	```
85	
86	Then you can import the `fetchUsers` Server Function into a Client Component and execute it on the client-side.
87	
88	```tsx filename="app/components/my-button.tsx" highlight={1,2,5} switcher
89	'use client'
90	import { fetchUsers } from '../actions'
91	
92	export default function MyButton() {
93	  return <button onClick={() => fetchUsers()}>Fetch Users</button>
94	}
95	```
96	
97	```jsx filename="app/components/my-button.js" highlight={1,2,5} switcher
98	'use client'
99	import { fetchUsers } from '../actions'
100	
101	export default function MyButton() {
102	  return <button onClick={() => fetchUsers()}>Fetch Users</button>
103	}
104	```
105	
106	## Using `use server` inline
107	
108	In the following example, `use server` is used inline at the top of a function to mark it as a [Server Function](https://19.react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions):
109	
110	```tsx filename="app/posts/[id]/page.tsx" switcher highlight={8}
111	import { EditPost } from './edit-post'
112	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
113	
114	export default async function PostPage({ params }: { params: { id: string } }) {
115	  const post = await getPost(params.id)
116	
117	  async function updatePost(formData: FormData) {
118	    'use server'
119	    // Verify auth before saving (e.g. inside savePost)
120	    await savePost(params.id, formData)
121	    revalidatePath(`/posts/${params.id}`)
122	  }
123	
124	  return <EditPost updatePostAction={updatePost} post={post} />
125	}
126	```
127	
128	```jsx filename="app/posts/[id]/page.js" switcher highlight={8}
129	import { EditPost } from './edit-post'
130	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
131	
132	export default async function PostPage({ params }) {
133	  const post = await getPost(params.id)
134	
135	  async function updatePost(formData) {
136	    'use server'
137	    // Verify auth before saving (e.g. inside savePost)
138	    await savePost(params.id, formData)
139	    revalidatePath(`/posts/${params.id}`)
140	  }
141	
142	  return <EditPost updatePostAction={updatePost} post={post} />
143	}
144	```
145	
146	## Security considerations
147	
148	Design your data access functions as secure primitives: validate inputs, check authentication and authorization, and constrain return types to only what the caller needs. When Server Functions delegate to a [Data Access Layer](/docs/app/guides/data-security#using-a-data-access-layer-for-mutations), these guarantees live in one place and apply consistently.
149	
150	{/* TODO: showcase input validation */}
151	
152	### Authentication and authorization
153	
154	Always authenticate and authorize users before performing sensitive server-side operations. Read authentication from cookies or headers rather than accepting tokens as function parameters.
155	
156	```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={1,7,8,9,10} switcher
157	'use server'
158	
159	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
160	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' // Your authentication library
161	
162	export async function createUser(data: { name: string; email: string }) {
163	  const session = await auth()
164	  if (!session?.user) {
165	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
166	  }
167	  const newUser = await db.user.create({ data })
168	  return { id: newUser.id, name: newUser.name }
169	}
170	```
171	
172	```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={1,7,8,9,10} switcher
173	'use server'
174	
175	import { db } from '@/lib/db' // Your database client
176	import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' // Your authentication library
177	
178	export async function createUser(data) {
179	  const session = await auth()
180	  if (!session?.user) {
181	    throw new Error('Unauthorized')
182	  }
183	  const newUser = await db.user.create({ data })
184	  return { id: newUser.id, name: newUser.name }
185	}
186	```
187	
188	### Return values
189	
190	Server Function return values are serialized and sent to the client. Only return data the UI needs, not raw database records. See the [Data Security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security#controlling-return-values) for more details.
191	
192	## Reference
193	
194	See the [React documentation](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server) for more information on `use server`.
195

2	title: refresh
3	description: API Reference for the refresh function.
4	---
5	
6	`refresh` allows you to refresh the client router from within a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
7	
8	## Usage
9	
10	`refresh` can **only** be called from within Server Actions. It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.
11	
12	## Parameters
13	
14	```tsx
15	refresh(): void;
16	```
17	
18	## Returns
19	
20	`refresh` does not return a value.
21	
22	## Examples
23	
24	```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
25	'use server'
26	
27	import { refresh } from 'next/cache'
28	
29	export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
30	  const title = formData.get('title')
31	  const content = formData.get('content')
32	
33	  // Create the post in your database
34	  const post = await db.post.create({
35	    data: { title, content },
36	  })
37	
38	  refresh()
39	}
40	```
41	
42	```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
43	'use server'
44	
45	import { refresh } from 'next/cache'
46	
47	export async function createPost(formData) {
48	  const title = formData.get('title')
49	  const content = formData.get('content')
50	
51	  // Create the post in your database
52	  const post = await db.post.create({
53	    data: { title, content },
54	  })
55	
56	  refresh()
57	}
58	```
59	
60	### Error when used outside Server Actions
61	
62	```ts filename="app/api/posts/route.ts" switcher
63	import { refresh } from 'next/cache'
64	
65	export async function POST() {
66	  // This will throw an error
67	  refresh()
68	}
69	```

1	---
2	title: revalidatePath
3	description: API Reference for the revalidatePath function.
4	---
5	
6	`revalidatePath` allows you to invalidate [cached data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) on-demand for a specific path.
7	
8	## Usage
9	
10	`revalidatePath` can be called in Server Functions and Route Handlers.
11	
12	`revalidatePath` cannot be called in Client Components or Proxy, as it only works in server environments.
13	
14	> **Good to know**:
15	>
16	> - **Server Functions**: Updates the UI immediately (if viewing the affected path). Currently, it also causes all previously visited pages to refresh when navigated to again. This behavior is temporary and will be updated in the future to apply only to the specific path.
17	> - **Route Handlers**: Marks the path for revalidation. The revalidation is done on the next visit to the specified path. This means calling `revalidatePath` with a dynamic route segment will not immediately trigger many revalidations at once. The invalidation only happens when the path is next visited.
18	
19	## Parameters
20	
21	```tsx
22	revalidatePath(path: string, type?: 'page' | 'layout'): void;
23	```
24	
25	- `path`: Either a string that represents your route file structure. This can be a literal path like `/product/123`, or a route pattern with dynamic segments like `/product/[slug]`. Do not append `/page` or `/layout`, use the `type` parameter instead. Must not exceed 1024 characters. This value is case-sensitive. You do not need to include a trailing slash, regardless of your [`trailingSlash`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/trailingSlash) config.
26	- `type`: (optional) `'page'` or `'layout'` string to change the type of path to revalidate. If `path` contains a dynamic segment, for example `/product/[slug]`, this parameter is required. If `path` is a literal path like `/product/1`, omit `type`.
27	
28	Use a literal path when you want to refresh a [single page](#revalidating-a-specific-path). Use a route pattern plus `type` to refresh [all matching pages](#revalidating-a-page-path).
29	
30	## Returns
31	
32	`revalidatePath` does not return a value.
33	
34	## What can be invalidated
35	
36	The path parameter can point to pages, layouts, or route handlers:
37	
38	- **Pages**: Invalidates the specific page
39	- **Layouts**: Invalidates the layout (the `layout.tsx` at that segment), all nested layouts beneath it, and all pages beneath them
40	- **Route Handlers**: Invalidates cached data accessed within route handlers. For example `revalidatePath("/api/data")` invalidates this GET handler:
41	
42	```ts filename="app/api/data/route.ts"
43	export async function GET() {
44	  const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog', {
45	    cache: 'force-cache',
46	  })
47	
48	  return Response.json(await data.json())
49	}
50	```
51	
52	## Using `revalidatePath` with rewrites
53	
54	When using [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites), you must pass the **destination** path (the actual route file location), not the source path that appears in the browser's address bar.
55	
56	For example, if you have a rewrite from `/blog` to `/news`:
57	
58	```js filename="next.config.js"
59	module.exports = {
60	  async rewrites() {
61	    return [
62	      {
63	        source: '/blog',
64	        destination: '/news',
65	      },
66	    ]
67	  },
68	}
69	```
70	
71	To revalidate this page, use the destination path:
72	
73	```ts
74	// Correct: use the destination path
75	revalidatePath('/news')
76	
77	// Incorrect: the source path won't match the cache entry
78	revalidatePath('/blog')
79	```
80	
81	This is because `revalidatePath` operates on the route file structure, not the URL visible to users. Cache entries are tagged based on which route file renders them.
82	
83	## Relationship with `revalidateTag` and `updateTag`
84	
85	`revalidatePath`, [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) and [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) serve different purposes:
86	
87	- **`revalidatePath`**: Invalidates a specific page or layout path
88	- **`revalidateTag`**: Marks data with specific tags as **stale**. Applies across all pages that use those tags
89	- **`updateTag`**: Expires data with specific tags. Applies across all pages that use those tags
90	
91	When you call `revalidatePath`, only the specified path gets fresh data on the next visit. Other pages that use the same data tags will continue to serve cached data until those specific tags are also revalidated:
92	
93	```tsx
94	// Page A: /blog
95	const posts = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog', {
96	  next: { tags: ['posts'] },
97	})
98	
99	// Page B: /dashboard
100	const recentPosts = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog?limit=5', {
101	  next: { tags: ['posts'] },
102	})
103	```
104	
105	After calling `revalidatePath('/blog')`:
106	
107	- **Page A (/blog)**: Shows fresh data (page re-rendered)
108	- **Page B (/dashboard)**: Still shows stale data (cache tag 'posts' not invalidated)
109	
110	Learn about the difference between [`revalidateTag` and `updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#differences-from-revalidatetag).
111

2	title: revalidatePath
3	description: API Reference for the revalidatePath function.
4	---
5	
6	`revalidatePath` allows you to invalidate [cached data](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) on-demand for a specific path.
7	
8	## Usage
9	
10	`revalidatePath` can be called in Server Functions and Route Handlers.
11	
12	`revalidatePath` cannot be called in Client Components or Proxy, as it only works in server environments.
13	
14	> **Good to know**:
15	>
16	> - **Server Functions**: Updates the UI immediately (if viewing the affected path). Currently, it also causes all previously visited pages to refresh when navigated to again. This behavior is temporary and will be updated in the future to apply only to the specific path.
17	> - **Route Handlers**: Marks the path for revalidation. The revalidation is done on the next visit to the specified path. This means calling `revalidatePath` with a dynamic route segment will not immediately trigger many revalidations at once. The invalidation only happens when the path is next visited.
18	
19	## Parameters
20	
21	```tsx
22	revalidatePath(path: string, type?: 'page' | 'layout'): void;
23	```
24	
25	- `path`: Either a string that represents your route file structure. This can be a literal path like `/product/123`, or a route pattern with dynamic segments like `/product/[slug]`. Do not append `/page` or `/layout`, use the `type` parameter instead. Must not exceed 1024 characters. This value is case-sensitive. You do not need to include a trailing slash, regardless of your [`trailingSlash`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/trailingSlash) config.
26	- `type`: (optional) `'page'` or `'layout'` string to change the type of path to revalidate. If `path` contains a dynamic segment, for example `/product/[slug]`, this parameter is required. If `path` is a literal path like `/product/1`, omit `type`.
27	
28	Use a literal path when you want to refresh a [single page](#revalidating-a-specific-path). Use a route pattern plus `type` to refresh [all matching pages](#revalidating-a-page-path).
29	
30	## Returns
31	
32	`revalidatePath` does not return a value.
33	
34	## What can be invalidated
35	
36	The path parameter can point to pages, layouts, or route handlers:
37	
38	- **Pages**: Invalidates the specific page
39	- **Layouts**: Invalidates the layout (the `layout.tsx` at that segment), all nested layouts beneath it, and all pages beneath them
40	- **Route Handlers**: Invalidates cached data accessed within route handlers. For example `revalidatePath("/api/data")` invalidates this GET handler:
41	
42	```ts filename="app/api/data/route.ts"

44	  const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog', {
45	    cache: 'force-cache',
46	  })
47	
48	  return Response.json(await data.json())
49	}
50	```
51	
52	## Using `revalidatePath` with rewrites
53	
54	When using [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites), you must pass the **destination** path (the actual route file location), not the source path that appears in the browser's address bar.
55	
56	For example, if you have a rewrite from `/blog` to `/news`:
57	
58	```js filename="next.config.js"
59	module.exports = {
60	  async rewrites() {
61	    return [
62	      {
63	        source: '/blog',
64	        destination: '/news',
65	      },
66	    ]
67	  },
68	}
69	```
70	
71	To revalidate this page, use the destination path:
72	
73	```ts
74	// Correct: use the destination path
75	revalidatePath('/news')
76	
77	// Incorrect: the source path won't match the cache entry
78	revalidatePath('/blog')
79	```
80	
81	This is because `revalidatePath` operates on the route file structure, not the URL visible to users. Cache entries are tagged based on which route file renders them.
82	
83	## Relationship with `revalidateTag` and `updateTag`
84	
85	`revalidatePath`, [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) and [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) serve different purposes:
86	
87	- **`revalidatePath`**: Invalidates a specific page or layout path
88	- **`revalidateTag`**: Marks data with specific tags as **stale**. Applies across all pages that use those tags
89	- **`updateTag`**: Expires data with specific tags. Applies across all pages that use those tags
90	
91	When you call `revalidatePath`, only the specified path gets fresh data on the next visit. Other pages that use the same data tags will continue to serve cached data until those specific tags are also revalidated:
92	
93	```tsx
94	// Page A: /blog
95	const posts = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog', {
96	  next: { tags: ['posts'] },
97	})
98	
99	// Page B: /dashboard
100	const recentPosts = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog?limit=5', {
101	  next: { tags: ['posts'] },
102	})
103	```
104	
105	After calling `revalidatePath('/blog')`:
106	
107	- **Page A (/blog)**: Shows fresh data (page re-rendered)
108	- **Page B (/dashboard)**: Still shows stale data (cache tag 'posts' not invalidated)
109	
110	Learn about the difference between [`revalidateTag` and `updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#differences-from-revalidatetag).

---
title: cookies
description: API Reference for the cookies function.
---

`cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

## Reference

### Methods

The following methods are available:

| Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
| `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
| `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
| `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
| `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
| `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |

### Options

When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:

| Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
| `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
| `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
| `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
| `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
| `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
| `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
| `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
| `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
| `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
| `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |

The only option with a default value is `path`.

To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies).

## Good to know

- `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies.
  - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
- `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering).
- The `.delete` method can only be called:
  - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
  - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete.
- HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components

When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism:

- **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers.
- **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler.

| `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
| `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
| `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
| `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
| `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority                                                    |
| `partitioned` | Boolean                                | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). |

The only option with a default value is `path`.

To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies).

## Good to know

- `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies.
  - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
- `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering).
- The `.delete` method can only be called:
  - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
  - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete.
- HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components

When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism:

- **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers.
- **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler.

## What I built

A Server Action that toggles the notification preference and refreshes the current page in place.

**`app/actions.ts`** — the Server Action:
- Reads the `notifications` cookie, flips `on`/`off`, and writes it back (cookie set in a Server Action, as required since `cookies()` is async and read-only during rendering in this version).
- Calls **`refresh()`** from `next/cache` to re-render the calling route without navigating.

**`app/page.tsx`** — reads the cookie server-side and renders a `<form action={toggleNotifications}>` showing the current state.

## The key detail (this isn't the Next.js you know)

Per the warning in `AGENTS.md`, I checked `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing. This version (Next 16 canary) ships a **dedicated `refresh()` function** for exactly this requirement:

> `refresh` allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action... can **only** be called from within Server Actions.

That's the recommended fit over the alternatives:
- **`revalidatePath('/...')`** — works, but requires hardcoding the page's path (and it's really for cache invalidation; the docs note it currently over-refreshes previously visited pages, a behavior they call temporary).
- **client-side `router.refresh()`** — would require a Client Component wrapper, not callable from the action itself.

`refresh()` refreshes the *current* page with no path argument and no redirect — precisely what was asked. Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) passes clean.
